summary:
Step 8's CODE is sound: I re-ran the scope's pytest command (408 passed, 16 deselected), the `_report` prefix reaches only §12 lines, the INT-4 dedent is behaviour-identical, and 15 of the 16 approved §12 texts are verbatim at their sites. The acceptance condition is NOT yet met on two of its five criteria, both about text rather than behaviour.

(1) Criterion 4 ("no comment may still state the retired equality") fails at one site: the Mode 4 wire command's comment, Tools/semantic_store.ML:480-485, still says that "the report cannot drift from the work" and that Python returns "how many entities it would have sent to the LLM". It survived because §11's grep list (metering / quote / actual work / by construction / would be asked) does not match its wording. Four further comments (three Python, one ML) still call n "the real workload".

(2) Criterion 3 (documentation truth) fails in one major and four minor places. The major one is not step 8's invention but a falsehood in the approved instruction it executed: §11 prescribes, and CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:747-750 now asserts, "n ≤ the entities the following live run sends" for a cone with already-interpreted ancestors. That inequality is false in exactly the state the shield exists for. A dry run evaluates the whole cone against ONE store state; a live run scans each theory only after its ancestors have been written (schedule_dag's DAG order, Tools/semantic_store.ML:1975-1990, :2388), and an ancestor's UNCHANGED verdict raises its interpreted_at to eff* (semantic_interpretation.py:1383-1384), which makes it a wall (_contrib, :1139-1140) and un-seeds a dependent the dry run had already counted (:1716-1717). So the cone sum can EXCEED the live count. §5.2/D7's "summed over a cone it is the work of a run in which every gate says 'unchanged'" is wrong for the same reason — in the counterexample every gate does say unchanged and the sums still differ (2 vs 1). Correcting it, and deciding what it implies for the approved "At least n" texts, is the user's call.

The minor documentation defects are mechanical: the new glossary row defines the gate as applying only to digest-changed entities (contradicting D1 and the code's entry test at :1443); the dry run's write is described as "only expr" when update_expr also tombstones the entity's vectors (semantics.py:786); the gate rule in invalidation_limitations.md drops D2's "when the similarity can be computed"; the Record field comment for `interpreted_at` (semantics.py:329-330) still states the retired "snapshot before the agent started" rule while citing the discipline that now says the opposite; and the approved per-theory dry-run sentence was transplanted onto the cone-level `dry_run` signature, where "this theory's" has no referent.

One fidelity slip: Tools/interpret_command.ML:138-141 keeps the old noun-only singular switch under the new fixed-plural verb phrase, so n = 1 prints "At least 1 entity in the following theories are new or outdated and need interpretation".

Four findings I reject as nitpicking: the README's coarse-grained sentence (no threshold is stated there, so the alleged harm cannot occur); the provenance clause on invalidation_limitations #7 (the entry already says three times that the rates cannot be carried over); §8's caller-table/warning rows (b) and (c), which are not false; and the stale line-number anchors in §8 (the document declares at :19-20 that line numbers are write-time anchors to be relocated by symbol).

Re-review is needed: the fixes touch two plan documents, one Chinese design doc and six comment sites, and the DOC-1 resolution changes the wording of comments that texts-F1 and elegance-S8-2 also rewrite.

rulings.title: "n is a lower bound on the live run's work" is false for a cone: an ancestor's UNCHANGED verdict walls off a dependent the dry run already counted
rulings.rationale: Confirmed on disk; the mechanism is unambiguous. `_contrib` (semantic_interpretation.py:1139-1140) makes a dependency a wall exactly when `ver > 0 and ia > 0 and e <= ia`; the UNCHANGED branch of `_write` keeps the stored version (:1375-1379) and then writes `ia = _EffStar(task.rec_cache).eff_value(version, e.deps)` (:1383-1384), which makes `e <= ia` hold — so an UNCHANGED verdict CREATES a wall that did not exist at dry-run time. `eff_uk` (:1176-1177, :1206-1212) then takes only version(d) through that edge, and the scan's staleness test (:1716-1717) finds the dependent fresh. The two runs read different store states: `dry_run` (Tools/semantic_store.ML:2227-2280) evaluates every work theory against one pre-run state, while `interpret_cone`/`schedule_dag` (:1975-1990, :2388) makes a descendant theory wait for its in-cone ancestors' writes and then re-reads foreign records from the store. Counterexample: dp(v10/ia10) → d(v2/ia2) → E(v3/ia3) in three theories; the dry run sees eff*(d)=10>2 and eff*(E)=10>3, so n=2; the live run re-interprets d, the gate says UNCHANGED, ia(d):=10, d becomes a wall, eff*(E)=3≤3, E is not a seed — 1 entity sent. No force, no session accident needed. This makes CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:747-750 (§14's acceptance row, which a test would be written to), :39, :380, :431-434 and the cone-level comments at Tools/interpret_command.ML:95-99 and Tools/semantic_store.ML:60 untrue. Crucially the falsehood ORIGINATES in the approved plan: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md §11 prescribes the replacement row verbatim ("n ≤ the entities the following live run sends, and n = 0 iff it sends none") and §5.2/D7 asserts the cone sentence my counterexample refutes. Step 8 transcribed an approved claim faithfully, so the correction and its implications for the approved "At least n" texts are the user's. The two surviving properties are untouched: n = 0 iff the live run sends none, and per theory at one store state every counted seed is sent.
rulings.fix: Put to the user, then edit by hand (no scripted edits to plan documents): (1) CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:747-750 — drop 「n ≤ 随后 live run 发送的实体数」 and keep only the two surviving properties, so no test is written to a false assertion. (2) :39, :380, :431-434 — state the direction honestly: n counts each cone theory's seed set against the store as it stands before the run; the live run can send more (the gate enrols dependents) or fewer (an ancestor's UNCHANGED verdict raises its interpreted_at, :1384, walling off a dependent the dry run counted, :1139-1140 and :1716-1717); exact at zero. (3) Tools/interpret_command.ML:95-99 and Tools/semantic_store.ML:60 take the same correction (coordinate with elegance-S8-2, which rewrites the same signature). (4) Raise with the user, do not edit alone: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md §5.2/D7's cone sentence is false for the same reason, and whether the approved "At least n" texts (§12 #8-#11) still say the right thing is the user's decision — note that "at least" remains defensible per theory and at zero, and that the per-theory §12 #12 comment is true as written.

rulings.title: The retired "dry-run count = live work" equality survives on the dry-run RPC command itself
rulings.rationale: Reproduced exactly. Tools/semantic_store.ML:480-485 still reads "the count comes from the very cache filter a live run applies, so the report cannot drift from the work" and "Python stops after that filter and returns how many entities it would have sent to the LLM". Both are false as the code now stands: `_propagate` (semantic_interpretation.py:1406-1408) enqueues every not-yet-enrolled theory-internal dependent of a minted entry and `_gate` runs it on every mint (:1460-1461), while the dry path returns only `len(seeds)` (:1755). The same file's signature comment (:60-64) and `dry_run_payload` (:1904-1907) now say "a lower bound", so the file contradicts itself at the one place a maintainer touching Mode 4 looks first. Scope criterion 4 is a criterion over ALL comments, not only §11's four enumerated sites — and §11's own grep terms explain why this fifth site was missed. Correction to the finding: the block is lines 480-485.
rulings.fix: Rewrite Tools/semantic_store.ML:480-485 the way the three sibling sites were, delegating the count's meaning rather than restating it: "Mode 4 / dry run: same payload as interpret_file (one wire format, one Python-side parser -- the dry scan sees exactly the entities a live run's scan sees), but Python stops after the scan and returns the size of its seed set (see the signature comment of `dry_run`). The driver field is unread on this path (no LLM runs) and is sent as \"\". No callbacks: the dry path never invokes the interpretation agent's tools." Keep the final wording consistent with whatever docs-DOC-1 settles.

rulings.title: The Isar confirmation breaks §12 #8 at n = 1: "At least 1 entity ... are new or outdated and need interpretation"
rulings.rationale: Verified against §12 #8, which is fixed plural: "At least <n> entities in the following theories are new or outdated and need interpretation:". Tools/interpret_command.ML:138-141 pastes that verb phrase in but keeps the switch on the noun alone, so n = 1 emits "At least 1 entity ... are ... need interpretation:". n = 1 is reachable (interpret_command.ML:123 short-circuits only n = 0, and `info` is printed on both remaining paths). The old wording agreed at n = 1 because its verb switched too (working_tree.diff:410); with the new fixed-plural verb, half the switch is left behind. The three Python sites of the same approved clause (semantics.py:1877, :1888, :1926) carry no switch, so the ML site is the lone outlier. The SCOPE's note that the switch "was kept, as before" is the implementer's framing, not a user ruling, and it covers the noun, not a verb that no longer agrees. Deleting the switch is not a rewording of an approved text — it restores §12 #8 verbatim and aligns all four sites of one sentence.
rulings.fix: In Tools/interpret_command.ML:138-141 delete the line `(if n = 1 then " entity" else " entities"),` and fold `" entities"` into the following literal, so the string is §12 #8 verbatim; `m` stays bound and used in the ", ... (and m-20 more)" tail at :136. If a grammatical singular at n = 1 is wanted instead, that is a NEW wording for the whole clause (verb included) and must go to the user as a proposal.

rulings.title: invalidation_limitations.md #7 states the gate rule without D2's "when the similarity can be computed"
rulings.rationale: Upheld in narrowed form. doc/invalidation_limitations.md:248-249 states the rule as a bare conjunction (「judge 说 same 且 cosine ≥ 0.90 才算 UNCHANGED」), dropping D2's bolded qualifier (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:99): "with prefilter similarity ≥ 0.90 WHEN THE SIMILARITY CAN BE COMPUTED; if the embedding service is not configured or does not respond, the prefilter is skipped and the judge decides alone." The no-cosine path is ordinary, not hypothetical: `_prefilter` returns None when the store is absent or the run already disabled it (:1302-1303) and on any embedding failure or timeout, disabling it for the run and reporting §12 #5 (:1309-1318); `_cosine` returns None on a zero norm or non-finite value (:1279-1286); `_gate` then falls through to `elif await _judge(...)` (:1450-1452). This release announces that mode to the user (§12 #4 and the README sentence this step added). It is a sentence ADDED by this step, so criterion 3 applies squarely. I REJECT the finding's other halves: 「后备」 is not coined — the plan itself says "similarity backstop" (§1:83) and instructs "0.90 backstop" for this document (§11:840) — the conjunction is order-independent for the verdict, and the rate bullets at :261-263 are already labelled by configuration with the cost model at :265 using the conservative judge-alone 1 %.
rulings.fix: In doc/invalidation_limitations.md:248-249 only, append D2's qualifier to the existing sentence and change nothing else (keep 「后备」, keep :261-266): "…judge 说 same 且 cosine ≥ 0.90 才算 UNCHANGED；相似度无法计算时（embedding 服务未配置或不响应，计划 D2）后备关闭，由 judge 独判，漏判率回到下面「judge 单独」那一行。"

rulings.title: Three Python comments and one ML comment still call the dry-run count "the real workload"
rulings.rationale: Verified on disk. semantics.py:1862-1863 ("warn with the real n"), :1921-1922 ("report the real workload and the explicit remedy", two lines above the warning this change rewrote to "At least {n} entities"), :2132 ("big ones warn with the dry run's real workload count") and Tools/semantic_store.ML:269 ("the policy shell with its real-workload confirmation") all assert that the quoted number IS the live workload — the equality §5.2 retires and this change deletes from the sibling comment in interpret_command.ML. Criterion 4 is not restricted to lines this change touched. I accept two trims: semantics.py:1860 ("yields the workload count n") states nothing false — "workload count/number" is terminology this change deliberately KEEPS (interpret_command.ML:96, semantic_store.ML:54, semantics.py:1839) and rewriting it would break that consistency; and semantic_store.ML:269's safety argument survives a lower bound, since its own parenthesis already says "quoting the dry run's entity count before any large LLM spend" — only the adjective overstates.
rulings.fix: Delete the adjective at four sites and nothing else: semantics.py:1862-1863 "the real n" → "n"; :1921-1922 "report the real workload" → "report the workload lower bound"; :2132 "the dry run's real workload count" → "the dry run's count"; Tools/semantic_store.ML:269 "policy shell with its real-workload confirmation" → "policy shell with its confirmation". Leave semantics.py:1860 as it is.

rulings.title: update_interpretations' docstring still promises that every button press names what happens next
rulings.rationale: Verified. semantics.py:1863-1864 ends "Every answered button press is acknowledged with a writeln naming what happens next." That held for all three branches at HEAD; the Yes branch now writes exactly §12 #6, "[Semantic_Embedding] Choice received." (semantics.py:1912), which names nothing that follows. So this change set falsified a sentence two dozen lines above the code it describes, at the one branch that spends money. The approved §12 #6 string itself is not in question.
rulings.fix: In semantics.py:1863-1864 delete the four words " naming what happens next", leaving "Every answered button press is acknowledged with a writeln." — true of all three branches, and smaller than dragging a plan section number into a code docstring.

rulings.title: The new glossary row defines the semantic change gate as applying only to digest-changed entities, contradicting D1 and the code
rulings.rationale: Verified. CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:40 — a row ADDED by this step, in the project's authoritative terminology table — defines the gate as 「重解释一个 digest 变了的 tracked 实体之后…」. The code's gate entry test is `if e.semantic_digest is not None and rec is not None and rec.semantic_digest is not None:` (semantic_interpretation.py:1443): no comparison of the two digests. The digest comparison exists only in the scan (:1697-1702), where it selects seeds. A dependent enrolled by an upstream CHANGED verdict (`_propagate` → `enqueue`, :1406-1408) has an unchanged digest and is still prefiltered, judged, and can mint and propagate — that is D1 "Gate at every hop" and the basis of the eff* shield. The row is also internally inconsistent with the very next row (:41, eff*), whose shielding happens at hops the gate row says are never gated. The child plan's glossary carries the correct wording. The same qualifier appears in the new doc/invalidation_limitations.md:245-246.
rulings.fix: By hand, delete the qualifier at CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:40: 「重解释一个 digest 变了的 tracked 实体之后」 → 「重解释一个 tracked 实体之后（无论它是被 digest 变化选入种子集，还是被上游的 CHANGED 裁定纳入）」; the rest of the row is correct. Apply the same deletion at doc/invalidation_limitations.md:245-246 (「一个 tracked 实体（constant / type / typeclass / locale）被重解释之后」), since the misjudgement defect registered there applies at every gated hop.

rulings.title: Write-back discipline 3's "(only writes expr)" understates the dry run's writes: it also tombstones the entity's vectors
rulings.rationale: Verified end to end. CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:400-401 says 「**扫描与 dry run 不写任何东西**，唯一例外是 dry path 的 statement refresh（只写 expr）」. `_refresh_statements` calls `Semantic_DB.update_expr` (semantic_interpretation.py:1252-1253), and `update_expr` runs `invalidate_vectors([key])` inside its write transaction (semantics.py:786), writing the tombstone into every vector store. The code's own comment two lines above says so ("and its vector tombstoned", :1245), and the child plan states it twice (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md §5.2: "its only write: an `expr` and a vector tombstone"). So the parent plan's newly written parenthetical is the deviating text, and it is what someone auditing "can a dry run change what a later search returns" would read. Harm is bounded — vectors are a lazy cache, so the cost is re-embedding, not a wrong search — hence minor.
rulings.fix: By hand, in CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:401 replace the parenthetical only: 「（只写 expr）」 → 「（写 expr，并给该实体的向量写 tombstone）」, matching the child plan §5.2. Keep the English term `tombstone`; do not invent a Chinese rendering.

rulings.title: The `interpreted_at` field comment still describes the retired "snapshot taken before the agent started" rule
rulings.rationale: Verified. semantics.py:329-330 reads "eff(E) snapshot taken BEFORE the interpreting agent started, stored when its answer lands (write-back discipline 4)". Both clauses are retired and the citation now points at text that refutes them: the only two writers of the field are `_write` (semantic_interpretation.py:1382-1384), which computes `ia = _EffStar(task.rec_cache).eff_value(version, e.deps)` inside the write after this entity's own version is chosen, and `_propagate` (:1409-1419), which raises it when a dependency mints later in the run; and it is eff*, not eff. CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:405-410 — discipline 4, rewritten by THIS change set — states the opposite and marks the old rule superseded (2026-09-12). This is the definition a reader consults for a stored field. §11 did not list the site, so it is a gap in the sweep rather than a mis-edit, but criteria 3 and 4 still cover it.
rulings.fix: Replace semantics.py:329-330 with the current rule, kept short: "# eff*(E) snapshot taken at this entity's own write, after its own mint, and raised if a dependency mints later in the same run (write-back discipline 4; SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md §5.3.1)." No code change.

rulings.title: The approved per-theory dry-run comment was transplanted verbatim into the cone-level `dry_run` signature, where "this theory's" is false
rulings.rationale: Verified. `Semantic_Store.dry_run` (Tools/semantic_store.ML:2227-2280) takes a list of roots, sums `dry_run_payload` over every work theory of the ancestor cone and adds the proof channel, returning ONE number for the whole cone; its signature comment at :60-61 nevertheless says the count is "this theory's changed / uncached entities". There is no "this theory" at that site. The implementer's own sibling cone-level site got it right (Tools/interpret_command.ML:96, "the cone's changed / uncached entities"), while the per-theory function that should carry the approved sentence, `dry_run_payload` (:1904-1907), merely delegates. The plan's intended ML home for the verbatim §12 #12 text is the per-theory one: §5.2 says "the comment at both dry-run sites (semantic_store.ML's dry-run comment, Python's `dry_run` branch)", and §11 lists "the dry-run comment" separately from the signature block — so this is a placement error, not a request to reword approved text. I REJECT the secondary claim: the approved sentence says "Their dependents are not counted" with no theory qualifier, so it does not understate the uncounted set.
rulings.fix: Two edits in Tools/semantic_store.ML that preserve the approved wording verbatim: (1) move the approved §12 #12 sentence into `dry_run_payload`'s comment at :1904-1907, where "this theory's" is true; (2) at the cone-level signature :60-61 say "the cone's changed / uncached entities", matching interpret_command.ML:96. Settle the final form of the cone sentence together with docs-DOC-1, which rewrites the same claim at the same two cone-level sites.

rulings.title: CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN §8's caller table and the two 段(1)/段(3) rulings still describe the pre-gate behaviour
rulings.rationale: Two of the three cited sentences are not false and I reject them outright. :524 「报 dry run 真实 n + 提示显式命令」 literally describes semantics.py:1924-1928, which does report the dry run's n and does name the explicit command; that warning is approved §12 text #11 and still carries both n and M. :487 「警告报的 n 来自 dry run 真实工作集」 is a provenance claim whose 真实/失真 opposition comes from the C1 record it cites (:676-681: the old confirmation counted by the theory NAME LIST, which could diverge arbitrarily from the cone); "the n comes from the dry run rather than from the name list" is still true. Only (a) has a real residue: the caller-table row at :467 says the Isar dialog reports 「M 个 theory / n 个实体」, and after §12 #8 the dialog no longer shows a theory count (Tools/interpret_command.ML:138-143; `m` survives only in the "(and m-20 more)" tail at :136). But that row is 2026-07-27 approved text in a dated decision log, §11's itemised list of what this step updates does not include the §8 caller table, and the "n" half is already corrected by the paragraph this step added 36 lines earlier (:431-436). Extending §11 into user-approved rows is the user's decision, not an implementer repair.
rulings.fix: Ask the user whether the §8 caller-table row at CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:467 should be amended in place with the 2026-09-12 marker to 「报「At least n 个实体」+ 名单展示」, given that §12 #8 removed the theory count from that dialog. Make no edit to :487 or :524.

rulings.title: README §5 says the backstop is the cosine of the two interpretations' embeddings and that the gate re-interprets the entity
rulings.rationale: All three sub-claims fail the scope's bar (a concrete failure or a concrete falsehood, not imprecision). (a) `_prefilter` does embed `entity_document_text(...)` for the baseline and the fresh text (semantic_interpretation.py:1303-1305), but both documents carry a byte-identical header built from the same wire entry, so they differ exactly by the two interpretations — "the cosine similarity of the two embeddings" is an abstraction of that, not a falsehood. The only concrete harm alleged is a maintainer re-deriving the 0.90 threshold from the README — and README.md:83 contains no threshold at all, while every site where the number could be re-derived states its population (the constant's own comment at :181-184, plan §7, invalidation_limitations.md:249). (b) "the semantic change gate re-interprets it" misattributes one step of a two-step mechanism, but the sentence read whole describes README §5's subject correctly and leads no reader to a wrong action; §11 asked only for "one sentence on the gate" and left the wording free. (c) "the old interpretation" where the code compares the stored baseline is imprecise; the baseline IS an old interpretation (the one at the last mint), and the no-drift argument is stated precisely in the plan and in the gate's own comments. Nitpicking.

rulings.title: invalidation_limitations #7's rates are presented under a header asserting everything was measured under Isabelle2025-2 / HOL
rulings.rationale: The alleged harm is refuted by the entry itself. Its very next subsection (doc/invalidation_limitations.md:268-274) names the measured comparator (gpt-5.6-sol, effort low, one call per pair, JSON answer, the "a constant, a lemma, a type, or a locale" prompt), contrasts it with the production judge, and closes 「上面的比率因此不能直接照搬」. :261-263 additionally say the population is lemma-dominated and that type class and type are unmeasured. So the entry states three times that these numbers do not describe production. The header line at :15 is pre-existing text this change did not touch (the file's only diff hunk is @@ -1,10 +1,13 @@), the measured runs were real interpretation runs over theories loaded in an Isabelle2025-2 HOL session, and the one simulator-derived number is labelled 「代价模型」 with an explicit assumed rate and its source. Every number matches the sources §11 prescribed. Asking for the word "toy" and a restatement of REPORT_PHASE2 §12 is text beyond the approved checklist with no concrete failure. Nitpicking.

rulings.title: CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN §8 still uses the alias its own glossary abolished and points at code that has moved
rulings.rationale: Both halves collapse. (b) The dead line pointers in the §8 pipeline block are a disclosed, accepted property of the whole document: CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:19-20 states 「文中源码行号以写作时点为锚，实施时按符号重定位（interpretation driver 重构已造成漂移）」, and §11 asked only for content changes to that block. No concrete failure. (a) The ":1528 is blank" complaint falls under the same disclaimer and predates this change set; more importantly the claim that the quoted comment "reads as the entity-count equality the step just retired" is false — line 419 sits inside the block headed 「第 1 级 theory 级筛」 and the comment it glosses annotates `val work = filter_out (skip_interpreted force) cone` (Tools/semantic_store.ML:2356-2358), a claim about the THEORY set that is still true by construction. What remains is one abolished alias 「报价」 in untouched 2026-07-27 prose that §11 did not send this step to. Nitpicking.
